_comment: Per-model label canonicalisation for the MTG Jamendo 87-class genre model. Jamendo labels are lowercase glued compounds ('deephouse', 'hardrock', 'jazzfusion'). The .NET §5.1a normaliser doesn't split compounds — without remap entries the resolver finds no taxonomy match. Coverage map below was generated by /tmp/raytagger-remap-analysis/analyzer.py against the full 87-class vocabulary; see docs/PLAN_GENRE_CLASSIFICATION.md §4.0a.
_section_natural_matches: These labels match natively (no entry needed, listed here for documentation): ambient, downtempo, dubstep, funk, house, jazz, pop, rap, rock, soul, techno, trance. 12 of 87 hits without remap. The four glued-name forms below also need remap entries because the .NET normaliser doesn't split compounds.
_section_glued_taxonomy_names: Compounds that map directly to a top-level taxonomy genre. Without the space the resolver's whole-word regex misses them entirely.
_section_compound_to_parent: Glued compounds where the parent genre is unambiguous. Splitting them with a space lets the resolver find the parent. The substyle word becomes context (resolver searches it as subgenre too — e.g. 'Deep House' yields House+Deep).
_section_skipped_ambiguous: Labels deliberately NOT remapped — standalone words that could map to multiple taxonomy entries, or compounds where the dominant assignment isn't clear. Pass through; resolver drops them silently (no candidate emitted). User can add a mapping rule if they want one. Examples: dance (Indie Dance? generic?), disco (70s disco ≠ Disco House subgenre), dub (Dub Techno vs reggae dub), eurodance (Pop? Dance?), hard (Hard Techno? Hard Trance? Hard Rock?), indie (Indie Dance? indie rock?), industrial (Industrial Techno? industrial rock?), latin (standalone vs House subgenre), minimal (House/Techno/DnB subgenre), progressive (House/Trance subgenre), psychedelic (Psy Trance? psych rock?).
